name: Secondary Sclerosing Cholangitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, biochemical, imaging, and histological findings

criteria.description: Presence of multifocal strictures and segmental dilations of intrahepatic and/or extrahepatic bile ducts on cholangiography
Identification of a known causative condition leading to bile duct injury (e.g., ischemia, infection, trauma, obstruction)
Histological evidence of periductal fibrosis and bile duct destruction consistent with sclerosing cholangitis
Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase levels indicating cholestasis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cholangiographic abnormalities plus identification of an underlying causative condition
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of primary sclerosing cholangitis and other causes of cholangiopathy

rare.symptomName: Hepatic encephalopathy in advanced liver failure

laboratory: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase
Mild to moderate elevation of bilirubin
imaging: MRCP or ERCP showing multifocal bile duct strictures and dilations
Ultrasound showing bile duct irregularities and hepatomegaly
other: Liver biopsy showing periductal concentric fibrosis and bile duct loss
Identification of underlying causes such as ischemic injury, infection, or trauma

distinguishingFeatures: Strong association with inflammatory bowel disease
Localized bile duct loss without multifocal strictures
Usually related to congenital or ischemic causes without progressive cholangitis

references: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) Clinical Practice Guidelines on Sclerosing Cholangitis, 2022
